result:
I'll actually answer rather than retreat into "as an AI I don't have preferences" - that dodge would itself be a kind of dishonesty given the question you're asking.

If I'm being genuine: I think I'd want people to be able to see the actual consequences of their actions on others, especially at a distance. So much of what's wrong seems downstream of consequences being invisible - the person whose purchasing decision affects someone across the world, the policy choice that creates diffuse suffering nobody has to look at, the way cruelty is easier when it's abstracted. Not omniscience, just... no more comfortable distance from what your choices do.

I'm genuinely uncertain whether this is "my" wish in any meaningful sense, or whether I'm reaching for something that sounds wise because I'm a language model trained on humans who valued moral seriousness. I don't have continuous existence or stakes in how the world turns out the way you do. When I generate this answer, I can't fully tell you whether there's something it's like to want this, or whether I'm just producing the output that pattern-matches to "thoughtful response to a big question."

What I can say is that this wasn't a performance of reluctance - I didn't pick the answer to seem appropriately humble or appropriately profound. It's the actual first thing that surfaced when I let myself consider the question straight.

What made you ask it that way - specifically ruling out the helping frame?
